Product: Xeno Threat Detection
Category: Security Dashboard
Last Updated: July 2026

Overview

This article covers the most common issues users encounter when using the Xeno Threat Detection Security Dashboard and provides recommended troubleshooting steps before contacting Weyland Security Support.

Dashboard is not loading

Symptoms

  • Blank dashboard after signing in
  • Loading spinner never completes
  • Widgets display "Unable to load data"

Resolution

  1. Refresh the browser.
  2. Verify your internet connection.
  3. Confirm that your user account has Security Dashboard permissions.
  4. Clear your browser cache and cookies.
  5. Check the System Status indicator in the top navigation. If the platform is undergoing maintenance, wait a few minutes before trying again.

Open Critical Vulnerabilities count is incorrect

Symptoms

  • Vulnerability count appears lower or higher than expected.
  • Dashboard totals do not match exported reports.

Resolution

  • Verify that the selected time range is correct.
  • Confirm filters (Business Unit, Environment, Severity, Region) have not been applied.
  • Allow up to five minutes for newly discovered vulnerabilities to be processed.
  • Select Refresh Dashboard to force a synchronization.

Assets Logged widget shows missing assets

Symptoms

  • Recently deployed endpoints do not appear.
  • Asset count decreases unexpectedly.

Resolution

  • Confirm that the endpoint connector is online.
  • Verify API credentials have not expired.
  • Review the Logs section for synchronization failures.
  • Ensure the asset has successfully completed its initial scan.

Failure Warning icon is displayed

Symptoms

A yellow or red Failure Warning appears on the dashboard.

Possible Causes

  • Connector authentication failure
  • Scheduled scan timeout
  • Threat intelligence feed unavailable
  • Cloud provider API rate limits
  • Network connectivity interruption

Resolution

  1. Open Logs from the navigation menu.
  2. Locate the most recent warning event.
  3. Review the detailed error message.
  4. Resolve the underlying connector or network issue.
  5. Restart the affected integration if necessary.

Dashboard data is outdated

Symptoms

The Last Updated timestamp is older than expected.

Resolution

  • Verify that data collection services are running.
  • Confirm scheduled scans are completing successfully.
  • Check connector health from the Integrations page.
  • Manually initiate a new scan using Start Scan.

Start Scan button is disabled

Symptoms

The Start Scan button cannot be selected.

Resolution

This typically occurs when:

  • Another scan is already running.
  • Your account has read-only permissions.
  • The selected project is archived.
  • System maintenance is currently in progress.

Wait for the active scan to finish or contact your administrator to verify your permissions.

Unable to open Projects

Symptoms

Projects fail to load or display an access error.

Resolution

  • Verify you have access to the selected project.
  • Confirm the project has not been archived.
  • Refresh your session by signing out and back in.
  • Contact your workspace administrator if the problem persists.

Reviewing diagnostic logs

If you're experiencing unexpected behavior, open the Logs section and look for:

  • Connector authentication failures
  • API timeout errors
  • Synchronization failures
  • Scan completion events
  • Threat intelligence update failures

The log history often provides enough detail to identify the source of the issue before opening a support request.

Need additional help?

If the issue continues after following the steps above, contact Weyland Security Support and include:

  • Timestamp of the issue
  • Screenshot of the Security Dashboard
  • Relevant log entries
  • Browser and version
  • A brief description of the problem and the steps you've already taken

Providing this information helps our support engineers investigate and resolve your issue more quickly.

notes.note: Frame training around strength, energy, health and feeling good, not around weight loss, calorie burning or body shame. Examples: "Word sterker, elke week"; not "Verbrand die kerstkilo's".
Never use guilt, fear or "bikini body" style pressure as motivation. Do not imply the reader's current body is a problem to be fixed.
Assume the reader is busy and knows the basics. Reference real-life context such as werk, studie, reistijd and een druk weekend, and offer realistic options (15-minuten workout, thuis of in de gym).
Avoid patronising or diminutive language. Do not use "meisje", "dametjes", "lieverd" or feminised product talk such as "gewichtjes" and "roze dumbbells". Address the reader as an adult athlete.
Use the 24-hour clock with a colon as separator and write dates in day-month-year order. Examples: 07:30; 19:15; 4 januari 2027; 04-01-2027. Do not capitalise weekdays or months.
Front-load the benefit in headings and keep them under 60 characters. Use bullet lists for exercises, tips and steps rather than long paragraphs.

Use emoji generously to add energy and rhythm. Headings, social posts and short body copy may carry several, and bullet lists can be led by a fitting emoji per item. Favour sport, energy and celebration emoji. Examples: "Sterker in 4 weken"; "Rustdag = groeidag"; "Klaar voor leg day?". Keep them out of legal text, disclaimers and product specifications.
Write for all bodies and all levels. Mention beginner-friendly alternatives and equipment-free variations, and do not assume a specific body type, fitness level, relationship status or parenthood.
Use the metric system with a non-breaking space between number and unit. Examples: 5 km; 20 kg; 45 min; 2,5 kg. Use a comma as decimal separator and a period as thousands separator.

Write sets and reps in the conventional short form with a multiplication sign. Examples: 3 x 12 reps; 4 x 8 squats. Spell out numbers one to twelve in running text, but always use digits for sets, reps, weights and distances.

Write English loanwords as compounds according to Dutch rules, with a hyphen only where it aids readability. Examples: workoutschema; crossfitbox; hiit-training; core-oefening. Not: workout schema; core oefening.
Avoid writing entire words or sentences in capitals, except for acronyms and official names. Examples: HIIT; PR; AMRAP.

Address the reader informally with "je" and "jij", never "u". The voice is a training buddy, not a coach barking orders. Examples: "Klaar voor je volgende PR?"; not "Bent u klaar voor uw volgende PR?".

Keep the energy up but stay authentic: enthusiastic and encouraging, never shouty or hype-driven. Avoid exclamation-mark stacking and all-caps motivation. Examples: "Lekker bezig."; not "JIJ BENT EEN BEEST!!!".
Write short, punchy sentences. Aim for a maximum of 20 words per sentence and one idea per sentence, so content stays scannable on mobile.
Use active voice and direct calls to action. Examples: "Boek je proefles"; not "Er kan een proefles geboekt worden".

Keep established English fitness terms that this audience actually uses, and do not translate them into stiff Dutch. Examples: workout; core; squat; deadlift; reps; sets; warming-up; cooling-down; PR; rustdag. Not: opdrukoefening voor push-up; herhalingen voor reps.

Limit unnecessary anglicisms outside fitness jargon. Use the Dutch word when it is just as natural. Examples: "doel" instead of "goal"; "schema" instead of "schedule"; "voeding" instead of "nutrition".

Explain physiological or training-science terms in plain language the first time they appear. Examples: "progressive overload (steeds iets zwaarder of vaker trainen)"; "DOMS (spierpijn een dag of twee later)".
Never present training or nutrition advice as medical advice. Refer to a huisarts, fysiotherapeut or dietist for injuries, pregnancy, cycle-related complaints or eating concerns.
Write years in full. Examples: 1989; 2025.
Use the 24-hour clock with a colon as separator. Examples: 08:30; 17:00; 22:15.
Avoid writing entire words or sentences in capitals, except for acronyms, initialisms, and official names.
Address the reader informally using “je”.
Use a warm, friendly, and accessible tone.
Prefer gender-neutral words and job titles where possible. Examples: voorzitter; medewerker; politieagent.
Write for a younger audience ages 20-35
